bridges.description: Support God's existence through the cumulative force of the selected arguments.
Connect cosmic origin, fine-tuning and morality to a personal good creator.
Use resurrection and defeater-sensitive experience to support Christian theism.
Support fallible disbelief by arguing that the evidence fits better without God.
Challenge divine explanation through natural reality, moral realism and suffering.
Challenge sectarian experience and historical inference as reliable routes to truth.

sections.title: Cosmic origin and causation
sections.rationale: Whether all physical reality began, whether beginning requires a cause, and whether that cause is personal form Craig's primary cosmological route and Nugent's most sustained reply.

sections.title: Fine-tuning and design
sections.rationale: The life-permitting range, the proposed necessity/chance/design alternatives, and the random-observer objection form a distinct probabilistic design exchange.

sections.title: Divine mind, change and freedom
sections.rationale: The coherence of an unembodied creator, creation by a reportedly changeless being, emergence of consciousness, and foreknowledge versus freedom are distinct attribute questions.

sections.title: Evil and comparative probability
sections.rationale: The speakers separately dispute logical compatibility of God with evil and whether suffering, cosmic scale, and other facts are probabilistically more expected without God.

sections.title: Objective moral grounding
sections.rationale: The existence, genealogy, knowledge, and normative grounding of objective duties are disputed through divine nature, evolution, and impartial rational choice.

sections.title: Divine commands and moral application
sections.rationale: The Euthyphro extension, evil-God reversal, commanded killing, and deathbed repentance test whether the proposed divine moral order is nonarbitrary and just.

sections.title: Resurrection, experience and method
sections.rationale: The resurrection case, personal religious experience, comparative defeaters, and evidential method distinguish Christian theism and test its warrant.
